turns.content: Let S be a sum of reciprocal sines. Which identity could rewrite a reciprocal sine as a difference of cotangents?
Derive the identity csc(x)=cot(x/2)-cot(x) from standard double-angle formulas.
Apply the identity to all eleven terms and write the resulting cotangent expansion, showing the first several terms and the final term.
Sum that expansion by telescoping. Which intermediate cotangents cancel, and which two endpoint terms remain?
Check the indexing of the eleven doubled angles and the first and last terms of the expansion. Have any endpoints been omitted?
Use cotangent's 180-degree period to reduce the final endpoint and express S in terms of cot(4 degrees) and tan(2 degrees).
Simplify that acute-angle expression exactly with a common denominator and write S as a single reciprocal sine.
Hence determine the acute angle alpha satisfying S=1/sin(alpha), and explain why the acute solution is unique.
